scenes.headline: How one line splits a noisy gradient in two
scenes.sub: Soft multi-token prediction, checked in float64
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Slope! Extra prediction heads help a language model learn, but their gradient hides two signals. One line keeps the useful one. We checked that it is exact.

scenes.label: What's new here
scenes.text: The extra heads' gradient is two parts: a pull toward the model's own next-token distribution, and noise from the one token sampled.
scenes.mark: noise from the one token sampled
scenes.say: Each extra head gets a pull toward the model's own next-token distribution, plus noise from whichever single token happened to be sampled.

parts.say: Plain training sends back the hard gradient.

parts.note: pull toward the model's own prediction
parts.say: It equals a K L term, the pull toward the model's own prediction.
Plus a residual that depends on the sampled token. Nothing is approximated.

steps.say: Both kinds of hidden state read from one trunk and through one shared output head.
Add the stop-gradient copy of the extra head's state, minus the state itself, to the next-token state. In the forward pass that adds zero.
In the backward pass it routes the residual back with a minus sign. The trunk receives only the K L gradient.
This is the paper's diagram. Red arrows carry cross-entropy gradients, the blue arrow carries the K L gradient.
The straight-through route hands the next-token gradient to the extra heads.

scenes.label: random cases where the routed gradient matched the explicit K L gradient
scenes.say: We tested it on three hundred random cases in float sixty-four. Every one matched the explicit K L gradient to rounding.

scenes.title: Output-head rank, 167M models
scenes.note: effective rank of the logit map, at most 512
scenes.say: On the authors' released small models, standard training lowers the output head's effective rank. The soft version stays close to the next-token baseline.

scenes.text: The sampled-token noise never shrinks with training. Soft-MTP keeps the pull toward the model's own predictions.
scenes.say: The noise from the sampled token never shrinks. Keep the pull toward the model's own predictions, and drop the noise.

recap: One line keeps only the pull.
No extra parameters, almost no cost.
scenes.say: Recap. The gradient splits exactly. One line keeps only the useful part. It adds no parameters and almost no cost.
